meaning.zh:
“好奇害死猫”。意思是过度的好奇可能会导致麻烦或危险。

这个短语的根源可以追溯到16世纪的英国剧作家Ben Jonson，他在戏剧中提到了这个概念。后来，这个短语在英语世界中流传开来，用以告诫人们不要过分好奇，因为过度的探究可能会带来不必要的麻烦或危险。
meaning.en: This phrase can be traced back to the 16th century British playwright Ben Jonson, who mentioned a similar idea in his plays. Later, this phrase became commonly used in the English-speaking world to warn people that excessive curiosity can lead to trouble or danger.

lines.en: I was going to ask about his personal life, but then I thought, *curiosity killed the cat*.
lines.zh: 我原本想问问他的私生活，但后来想起好奇害死猫。

lines.en: You shouldn't go poking around in his room, remember, *curiosity killed the cat*.
lines.zh: 你不应该到他房间里到处翻找，记住，好奇害死猫。

lines.en: She decided not to investigate the noise any further, thinking *curiosity killed the cat*.
lines.zh: 她决定不再追究那个噪音，想着好奇害死猫。
